title: Suggestions — review first, choose a path, then implement
rule: Nothing in this file has been implemented by this session. These are options.
Each suggestion names what it costs, what it risks and what would have to be true for it to be right.
The decision column is deliberately blank. It is the owner's answer, and until it is written the row stays 'undecided'.
owner_decisions: D-1 Which register is authoritative when the three disagree (see Q02).
D-2 Whether to buy or licence a price series, and under which terms (Q03/Q13).
D-3 Whether raw captures may be served publicly, or must move to a private store (Q14).
D-4 Which namespaces are live and which are history (Q18).
D-5 Whether one repo-level verifier replaces the 40 per-namespace verifiers (Q17).

rows.suggestion: Make this workspace the single front door and mark every other NFL namespace as either live or history, in one column.
rows.fixes: Q18 — 40 landing pages with no way to tell which is current.
rows.cost: One column in nfl-desk/data/census.json plus one nav edit; no data changes.
rows.risk: Demoting a namespace another session still considers live. Mitigation: nothing is deleted, only unlinked from the front door.
rows.decide_when: After the census table has been read once by the owner.
rows.would_change_our_mind: A namespace that is both verifier-green and read by a live page, yet unlinked, would argue for keeping it on the front door.

rows.suggestion: Adopt the round-2 rule ('met requires an artifact path that exists and an official source that supports the claim') as the only status rule, and retire the other two status columns to history.
rows.fixes: Q02 — 62 status disagreements across three registers.
rows.cost: One script change plus a verifier check that fails on an unresolvable evidence path.
rows.risk: Several rows currently marked implemented would drop to partial. That is the point, but it will look like regression.
rows.decide_when: As soon as the owner accepts that a lower honest number beats a higher unverifiable one.
rows.would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the round-2 downgrades were themselves wrong (e.g. a null market price that turns out to be populated elsewhere).

rows.suggestion: Settle the corpus before any further modelling: reconcile nfl-core's 272 rows to the official week pages, publish one settled-game list, and retire the 137/136/150 ambiguity.
rows.fixes: Q01 — three counts for the same season, and a brief that says 136.
rows.cost: One reconciliation pass over 18 week pages, machine-checkable afterwards.
rows.risk: The reconciled total will differ from every existing dashboard, which will break eight pages' captions at once.
rows.decide_when: Before any new ROI, Brier or gate number is published.
rows.would_change_our_mind: If the official week pages themselves disagree with the standings arithmetic, the ambiguity is upstream and must be reported, not resolved.

rows.suggestion: Make the availability capture the load-bearing dataset: daily Wednesday-to-kickoff pulls, raw HTML plus hash, an inactive-list capture 90 minutes before every kickoff, and a per-week row that says how many rows carried a designation.
rows.fixes: Q04, Q05, Q06, Q08 — no replayable injury series and no inactive evidence.
rows.cost: A scheduled job that already exists in skeleton form, plus storage; ~370 KB per capture today.
rows.risk: Storage growth and schema drift on the league's page. Mitigation: the existing manifest already records bytes and schema_ok per capture.
rows.decide_when: Before any injury or personnel feature is added to a model.
rows.would_change_our_mind: A published official inactive-list feed in machine-readable form would remove the scraping part of this.

rows.suggestion: Do not build any depth-based deficiency feature until one of three routes covers 32/32 clubs: club pages (31 today), Game Books, or an official snap-count source.
rows.fixes: Q07, Q08 — a matchup matrix would be built on 31 clubs and one image.
rows.cost: No build cost; it is a refusal. The cost is the feature that does not ship.
rows.risk: The most attractive feature on the brief stays unbuilt for another season.
rows.decide_when: Now — the brief itself already says not to build it before a route is verified.
rows.would_change_our_mind: A structured Houston depth feed, or snap counts for the current season.

rows.suggestion: Split every published correlation and every price column into an official block and a third-party block, each labelled, each carrying n and an interval, and keep them on separate pages.
rows.fixes: Q12, Q13 — third-party numbers sitting beside official ones.
rows.cost: One page split per namespace that publishes correlations; no recomputation.
rows.risk: Pages get longer and some currently 'complete' tables lose rows.
rows.decide_when: Before any strategy is ranked using a correlation.
rows.would_change_our_mind: A licence that makes the third-party series officially usable would let the blocks merge.

rows.suggestion: Run the leaderboard as a season-long shadow competition with posted rules, a pre-registration hash per strategy, and rewards defined in advance but not paid until a strategy clears its own required n.
rows.fixes: Q10 — 15 strategies, none reward-eligible, and no visible path to eligibility.
rows.cost: A weekly job that records forecasts before kickoff and a fixed scoring script.
rows.risk: An empty leaderboard for a season. That is also the honest outcome if nothing has skill.
rows.decide_when: Before the next week's fixtures, so the sample is prospective.
rows.would_change_our_mind: A strategy that reaches its pre-registered n and still cannot beat the control baseline would justify ending the competition rather than extending it.

rows.suggestion: Replace the 40 per-namespace verifiers with one repo-level verifier that runs every existing one, then adds the cross-namespace checks (status disagreement, corpus count, duplicate page count).
rows.fixes: Q17 — no gate fails when two files disagree.
rows.cost: One workflow file; every existing verifier already exits non-zero on failure.
rows.risk: A flaky peer verifier would block all unrelated work. Mitigation: run them per-namespace but aggregate the result into one required check.
rows.decide_when: After D-4 settles which namespaces are live.
rows.would_change_our_mind: Evidence that a peer verifier is itself wrong would mean fixing it first, not aggregating over it.

rows.suggestion: Publish the venue of every Week 11 fixture from the official game centre (city and stadium), and leave roof, surface and weather blank until an official designation is captured.
rows.fixes: Q16 — venue facts exist officially but are not published as data.
rows.cost: 13 game-centre reads per week; each prints Location and Stadium.
rows.risk: A venue name is a fact of the fixture, not a model input; publishing it must not be read as a conditions claim.
rows.decide_when: Before any totals strategy references conditions.
rows.would_change_our_mind: An official roof designation for all 32 stadiums would let the conditions columns be filled at the same time.

rows.suggestion: Keep the roster/turnover event stream (transactions, reserve list) as a first-class dataset and stamp every depth and availability row with the last roster event it has been checked against.
rows.fixes: Q09 — depth charts that still name players on reserve.
rows.cost: One join per capture; the transactions and reserve-list captures already exist.
rows.risk: Stamping requires a re-read of club pages, which is the expensive part.
rows.decide_when: Before a per-team 'starters out, replacements named' view is trusted.
rows.would_change_our_mind: If clubs published machine-readable depth charts with an as-of date, the stamp becomes a field copy instead of a re-read.
